skill.name: unit-testing-test-generate
skill.description: Generate maintainable unit test plans and starter test suites for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Java, and Go projects.
skill.summary: Creates framework-aware unit test outlines, mocks, coverage gap notes, and CI test commands.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown fences and TypeScript template literals in SKILL.md. One subprocess.run coverage example is kept as a confirmed issue because it runs a caller-provided command if implemented. No evidence found for prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: The coverage analyzer example executes a caller-provided test command.
remediation.suggestion: Use an allowlist of known test runners, pass arguments separately, and require user approval before running coverage commands.

remediation.issue: Generated test source may include names taken from analyzed code.
remediation.suggestion: Validate function, class, and component names before inserting them into generated test source.

content.value_statement: Writing complete unit tests is slow when projects use different languages and frameworks. This skill analyzes code structure and drafts focused tests, mocks, coverage notes, and CI commands.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes Python functions and classes to identify testable units.
Drafts pytest test classes with success, edge case, and error scenarios.
Drafts Jest suites for JavaScript and TypeScript functions.
Creates React Testing Library examples for render, state, interaction, and prop updates.
Suggests mock fixtures and coverage gap follow-up tests.
Lists CI test commands for pipeline integration.
limitations: Generated tests need review because assertions may be generic.
It cannot verify behavior without clear source code and expected outcomes.
Coverage analysis examples may require approved local test commands.
It is not designed for full integration or end-to-end testing.

use_cases.title: Backfill Service Tests
use_cases.description: Generate pytest or Jest coverage for existing functions before refactoring.

use_cases.title: Validate UI Components
use_cases.description: Draft React Testing Library cases for render states, interactions, and prop changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify coverage gaps and create follow-up tests for risky files.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Unit Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one source file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate unit tests for this file. Use the project test framework. Cover normal input, empty input, and expected errors. Explain each scenario briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Add Edge Cases and Mocks
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for stronger behavior coverage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module and draft unit tests. Include edge cases, dependency mocks, and meaningful assertions. List any behavior assumptions that need confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Component Test Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced frontend request for React components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create React component test scenarios for this component. Cover render state, user interaction, prop updates, and accessible queries. Avoid brittle selectors.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Coverage Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this coverage summary and source code to propose targeted unit tests. Prioritize risky gaps. Suggest CI commands, but do not run them.

output_examples.input: A Python module with public functions and validation branches.
output_examples.output: A pytest test plan covering valid inputs, empty inputs, expected errors, and recommended mock fixtures.

output_examples.input: A React component with props, state, and a button interaction.
output_examples.output: A React Testing Library scenario list for initial render, user clicks, prop updates, and accessible queries.

output_examples.input: A coverage report showing missed lines in several files.
output_examples.output: A prioritized gap list with targeted test ideas and CI command notes for approved execution.

best_practices: Provide source code, framework, expected behavior, and known edge cases.
Review generated assertions so each test checks a meaningful outcome.
Run tests in an approved environment before adding them to CI.
anti_patterns: Do not accept generic tests that only check for non-null results.
Do not generate tests without understanding dependencies and side effects.
Do not run coverage commands that have not been approved.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers pytest, Jest, React Testing Library, JUnit, and Go testing patterns.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It drafts tests and may suggest commands. Run commands only in an approved local or CI environment.

faq.question: Can it handle private codebases?
faq.answer: Yes, when the code is available in the current workspace and allowed for analysis.

faq.question: Will generated tests be perfect?
faq.answer: No. Review assertions, expected values, and mocks before committing generated tests.

faq.question: Can it create mocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest mock fixtures for external dependencies and repeated setup.

faq.question: Is it for integration testing?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on unit tests and may note when integration coverage is needed.
